 Judgment

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- from the respondents, for the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 01-08-2023 at about 4.30 a.m., the petitioner was passenger in a private bus bearing Reg. No.KA-51-AB-953 along with her mother-in-law and two minor children and were proceeding from Koppal towards Bengaluru, on NH- 48.

When the said bus was proceeding in between Sira and Tumkur, near Chikkanahalli Village, Sira Taluk, the driver of the said bus drove the same with high speed, in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the ongoing lorry from behind.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries all over her body.

Immediately after the accident, she was shifted to Government Hospital, Sira,
wherein she took first aid treatment and then she was shifted to People Tree Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein she took treatment as an in-patient.
Earlier to the accident, she was house wife doing all household works independently and also taking care of her two minor children and other family members.
But, due to the accidental injuries, she has become permanently disabled and thereby unable to do any work.
The Kallambella Police have registered the case against the driver of the said bus for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 338 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- with interest.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared through their counsel and filed their separate written statements.

sentences.text: 4. The respondent No.1 in his written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

He has contended that, the alleged accident has not occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of bus bearing Reg. No.KA-51-AB-953, but the same has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the lorry, who was not having control on the said road and suddenly stopped his vehicle without giving stop signal.
Due to which, the bus got dashed against the lorry, which was causing treat to the other road users and endangering the human life on that day.
He has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries sustained, medical expenses incurred and treatment taken by her.

He has admitted that, he is the R.C. owner of the bus bearing Reg. No.KA-51-AB-953 and the said vehicle is insured with the respondent No.2 vide policy No.1- 2HBQ2WPL/P400 and the same is valid from 21-08-2022 to 20-08-2023.
For the above denials and contentions, he has prayed to dismiss the petition.
5. Whereas, respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy to the bus bearing Reg. No.KA-51-AB-953 and liability to indemnify the respondent No.1, subject to the terms and conditions of the policy,
provisions of Motor Vehicles Act, valid and effective driving licence held by the driver of bus, valid registration certificate, fitness certificate and permit and also subject to the confirmation of Section 64VB of the Insurance Act.
It seeks protection under Section 147 and 149(2) of Motor Vehicles Act.
Further it is contended that, the petition is bad for non-compliance of provision under Sections 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.
Further it is contended that, the driver of the lorry were solely responsible for the alleged accident and the driver of the bus bearing Reg. No.KA-51-AB- 953 was no way responsible for the accident.

Further it is contended that, in the complaint and F.I.R.,
nowhere it is mentioned the name of petitioner.
After thorough investigation the police have filed the charge-sheet.
The petitioner name do not reflect or mentioned in the victim list.
It clearly goes to show that, the petitioner has not sustained injury in the alleged accident.

Further it is contended that the claim petition is liable to be dismissed for non-joinder of necessary parties, as the insured and insurer of the lorry and driver of the bus are not made party to the present proceedings.

Further it is contended that, at the time of accident the driver of the bus was not possessing valid and effective driving licence and the respondent No.1/owner of insured bus bearing Reg.
No.KA-51-AB-953 knowingfully well that his driver was not holding driving licence to drive the said vehicle, has willfully handed over his vehicle to the said driver to drive.

Further it is contended that,
the offending vehicle was not having proper and valid fitness certificate and permit to ply the said vehicle on the road.
Hence, the respondent No.1 has violated the terms and conditions of the policy and as such this respondent is not liable to indemnify the insured/respondent No.1.
Further, it has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries sustained, medical expenses incurred and treatment taken by her.
Further, it has sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
The compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

On meticulously going through the above police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 6, prima-facia it reveals that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending bus bearing Reg. No.KA-51-AB-0953 and dashing the same to an ongoing lorry from behind.
Due to said impact the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

The investigation officer in his final report, marked as Ex.P.6 has clearly stated that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending bus bearing Reg.
No.KA-51-AB-0953.
13.

At the outset, it is pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
involvement of bus bearing Reg. No.KA-51-AB-0953 in the said accident, issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.2 in respect of said vehicle and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.

But, the respondent No.1 & 2 have specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and taken specific defence that, the alleged accident has taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of ongoing lorry, who without having control on the said road has suddenly stopped his vehicle without giving any signal or indications.
Due to which the bus in which the petitioner was traveling got dashed against the said lorry.

Further it is contended that, the said accident has taken place solely due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of ongoing lorry and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of bus bearing Reg.
No.KA-51-AB-0953.
But, the respondents have failed to establish the said contentions.

They have neither adduced any evidence, nor they have produced any document to show that, at the relevant point of time of accident, the driver of ongoing lorry was driving the same in rash and negligent manner and the said accident has taken place due to his own rash and negligent driving.
Even, the respondents have not stepped into witness box to depose the above contentions on oath.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending bus bearing Reg. No.KA-51-AB-0953 and dashing the same to the lorry from behind.

Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from her mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of her evidence or which goes to show that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of ongoing lorry or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.

14. No.KA-51-AB-0953 and ongoing lorry.

When the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of ongoing lorry, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending bus bearing Reg. No.KA-51-AB-0953.

The P.W.3, who is the doctor who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the petitioner has sustained above injuries in the road traffic accident.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.3 in length, nothing worth has been brought out from his mouth, which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
On the other hand, there is no contrary or rebuttal evidence on record to disbelieve the above medical records of the petitioner.

Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that, the respondents No.1 and 2 have failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending bus bearing Reg. No.KA-51-AB-0953 and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

16. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

20. Towards loss of future income: In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove her age, the petitioner has produced the notarised copy of her Aadhar card, which is marked as Ex.P.7.
As per Ex.P.7, the date of birth of the petitioner is 07- 03-1990.
The accident has taken place on 01-08-2023 at about 4:30 a.m.
This clearly goes to show that, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident was 33 years.

Further, the P.W.3, who is the doctor who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered L1 compression fracture.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries sustained by the petitioner he found that, there is 30% permanent physical impairment in her L.S. Spine contributing to whole body disability.

Further, the Ex.P.5 wound certificate, Ex.P.8 discharge summary, Ex.P.9 radiology report, Ex.P.10 OPD slips, Ex.P.15 x-ray, Ex.P.19 case- sheet, Ex.P.20 OPD slip, Ex.P.21 is disability assessment form and Ex.P.22 x-ray clearly speaks that, the petitioner has suffered the above stated injury and for the said injury she has undergone surgery.
The P.W.3 has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, the petitioner has not suffered any disability and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability.

Further he has clearly admitted in his cross-examination that, at the time of discharge the treated doctor has not advised for any further treatment except medication, the complaints stated in his affidavit do not find place in any of the medical records of the petitioner, the implants are permanent, he has assessed only physical disability and not functional disability, he has not produced radiological report in support of his assessment, the petitioner can perform his day to day activities and continue her avocation with some difficulties.

Therefore, in such circumstances and taking into consideration the age of the petitioner, injury sustained, avocation of the petitioner, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence available on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the physical disability of 20% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.

Hence, in the instant case the disability of 20%
to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending bus bearing Reg. No.KA-51-AB-0953 the accident in question has taken place.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

ORDER The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.9,26,594/-, (Rupees nine lakh twenty six thousand five hundred and ninty four only), with interest at the rate of 6%
per annum, from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner.

However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.2 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.

Out of total compensation amount awarded in favour of petitioner, 30% of the compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be deposited in her name as fixed deposit in any nationalized bank for the period of three years, with liberty to draw the accrued interest periodically and the remaining 70% amount with proportionate interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner, through e- payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
